scope: P1 held-out direct-union probe versus frequency, gate-replay, shared-correction, and MTP baselines

test_split.opening_rule: Before the capture and scorer candidate is committed and reviewed, do not read any value from test records.npz or from a test-corresponding raw trace, capture, mapping, or derived artifact. The preserved split-isolation incident disclosed that NumPy previously materialized archive member names, shapes, and dtypes; therefore this is a value-isolation claim, not a literal never-opened claim.

held_out_isolation.already_observed: Archive member names, shapes, and dtypes only; NumPy materialized members while reporting that schema.
held_out_isolation.still_unseen: Test request IDs and case mapping, token positions, selected expert IDs, hidden-feature values, router logits/scores, baseline/probe predictions, targets, per-case metrics, and aggregate metrics.
held_out_isolation.embargo_scope: The test records.npz plus every test-corresponding row in the retained exact-router trace, future baseline captures, request/case mappings, manifests that reveal those mappings, and derived artifacts.
held_out_isolation.authorized_opener: After capture and scorer review, one hash-logged scorer invocation may atomically bind and open all test-corresponding sources. Synthetic fixtures and authorized training rows are the only pre-review execution inputs.
held_out_isolation.failure_rule: Any additional value-level test access before that reviewed opener is a gate failure and requires a replacement held-out split.

sources.frequency_training: Only the 55 train-fit requests and two grouped long-training shards already authorized by the P1 plan.
sources.probe_training: The exact 75 rank-32 states and training reports bound by the selected probe receipt; completed validation must independently retrain and exact-compare them.
sources.shared_correction_source: A fresh default-off diagnostic capture from the reviewed two-step correction implementation. It must emit a full stable 256-expert ranking, not only the existing top-8 PREDPAIR row.
sources.mtp_source: A fresh default-off diagnostic rollout from the model's bound MTP head plus rollback-safe target evaluation used only to observe predicted-token routes. It must not commit speculative target state or change target outputs.

common_event_contract.layers: Exact routed layers 4 through 77. Layer 3 is excluded for every method because the shared-correction comparator structurally predicts layer L from L-1 and has no layer-2 routed source.
common_event_contract.source_row: For every test request, select exactly the last eight token positions that have a complete K=8 same-request future window. Score those same eight positions at every common layer. A request with fewer than eight such positions is FAIL. This structural rule is fixed before request lengths or values are opened.
common_event_contract.target: The Boolean union of exact selected expert IDs at positions t+1 through t+K for K in {2,4,8}.
common_event_contract.pairing: Every method must score the identical ordered event keys for every K. Missing, extra, duplicated, reordered, or cross-request/layer rows are FAIL.

ranking_definitions.frequency: For each layer, count selected-expert occurrences only in authorized training rows; rank by descending count then ascending expert ID.
ranking_definitions.gate_replay: At source row (request,L,t), capture the production router's exact 256 effective F32 scores after sigmoid and exp_probs_b bias. Rank those captured score bits by descending value then ascending expert ID; do not recompute them in the acceptance scorer. The same current-state ranking predicts each future K union.
ranking_definitions.shared_correction: For source row (request,L,t), use the reviewed two-step predictor computed while executing layer L-1 at t: add that layer's shared-expert output to its post-attention residual, apply layer L RMSNorm and router, then capture and rank all 256 production effective F32 scores by descending value and ascending expert ID. The same corrected current-state ranking predicts each future K union.
ranking_definitions.mtp_rollout: This is an explicit hybrid main-head/MTP recurrence, because GLM-5.2 has one nextn block rather than a K-token MTP-only head. From an isolated session containing the exact source prefix through t, q1 is the greedy argmax of the target logits already produced at t; no known future test token is read. For j=1..8, evaluate qj with the target at position t+j and capture that token's full 256 effective F32 router scores at every common layer. Before evaluating qj, use hidden h[t+j-1] and qj in the bound one-step nextn block to produce q(j+1), except after j=8. Thus q2=MTP(h[t],q1), q3=MTP(h[t+1],q2), and so on. K=2 and K=4 are exact prefixes of the single K=8 rollout. For each K and expert, take the maximum captured effective score over q1..qK, then rank descending with ascending expert-ID ties. Every qj, route position t+j, hidden-state lineage, main-head/MTP provenance, and raw score bits are recorded; missing or misaligned steps are FAIL.
ranking_definitions.probe: Use the exact selected rank-32 head on the qualified int4 gate-input feature plus causal selected-expert history. Its separate K logits rank all 256 experts by descending value then ascending expert ID.

cost_accounting.required: Report parameters, incremental persistent bytes, peak temporary bytes, target expert bytes read, and synchronized completed inference time per source event for every non-frequency method. Persistent means bytes retained between tokens beyond the then-current serving configuration; temporary means the peak additional live allocation. Capture formatting and file writes may be excluded only through a separately measured paired arm, while score movement required by an online consumer remains included.
cost_accounting.timing_protocol: For each K and non-frequency method, run five fresh-server matched blocks on identical source events and order them with the campaign's frozen public-random arm scheduler. Time from required feature construction or isolated-session creation through device synchronization, prediction, any target evaluations and expert reads, required score movement, and teardown/disposal. Report every completed event, the unrounded mean, a request-paired 95% interval, and cold and warm results separately. Missing, timed-out, unequal, or unsynchronized arms are FAIL.
cost_accounting.mtp_interpretation: MTP rollout is an offline comparator unless an address-only online implementation avoids target expert reads. K-specific cost includes q1 argmax, seven-or-fewer MTP calls, all K target evaluations, target expert I/O, isolated-session prefix construction, synchronization, and disposal. Capture-only F32 file serialization is the only excluded component and must be measured separately. It cannot be described as free prefetch lookahead.
cost_accounting.shared_interpretation: Include normalization, all router matmuls, stable ranking/score movement, and synchronization required online. Use the already measured serving campaign failure as cost evidence in addition to capture-local timing; better recall does not erase its measured decode regression.
cost_accounting.equal_cost_rule: MTP is equal-cost to another method only if its upper 95% completed-time bound is no more than 1.05 times that method's lower 95% bound, its incremental persistent and peak temporary bytes are each no larger, and its target expert bytes read are no larger. MTP dominates only if it is equal-cost by all three dimensions and its recall point estimate is strictly higher in all nine K/budget cells. Otherwise report both methods on the Pareto table without folding the probe into MTP.

mtp_isolation_contract.mechanism: Run MTP capture in a standalone diagnostic engine process with its own graph, KV caches, MTP fields, and expert-cache namespace; never load or roll drafts in the authoritative target/control process. Disable the shared resident expert arena in the diagnostic process so no cache-residency state crosses the process boundary. Create a fresh diagnostic session for each structural source position, replay only the exact known prefix through t, execute the frozen hybrid recurrence, then destroy the session.
mtp_isolation_contract.future_data_rule: Only prefix tokens through t may seed the isolated session. Actual test tokens at t+1 or later are targets only and must never be inputs to q1 or later drafts.
mtp_isolation_contract.state_proof: The authoritative/control process is never attached to the diagnostic process or namespace. Before and after every diagnostic rollout, hash the control process's checkpoint, logits, dense/compact/indexer KV metadata and contents, MTP fields/caches, and cache-residency map and require no change. Continue a fixed suffix in that untouched control and in a separately fresh clean control; logits, greedy tokens, output bytes, checkpoint selection, and cache residency must be identical.
mtp_isolation_contract.failure_injection: Synthetic tests inject failure after each MTP call, target evaluation, route capture, and disposal stage. Every path must destroy the diagnostic session and leave the authoritative state and continuation identical.
mtp_isolation_contract.coverage: One K=8 rollout must produce the nested K=2 and K=4 prefixes. Missing drafts, partial layer scores, state drift, non-byte-identical continuation, or shrinking common coverage is FAIL.

router_score_conformance.scores: Capture all 256 effective F32 production-router score bits for gate-replay, shared correction, and every MTP-evaluated token. Reject NaN/Inf before ranking.
router_score_conformance.ranking: Rank captured scores directly by descending F32 value and ascending expert ID; do not recompute sigmoid or bias in the acceptance scorer.
router_score_conformance.production_check: For every event, the first eight experts of the scorer's stable full ranking must exactly equal the production router-selected IDs captured in that same event. Any mismatch is FAIL.
router_score_conformance.offline_recompute: CPU sigmoid(logit)+bias recomputation is diagnostic only and must bit-bind its implementation; it has no acceptance authority.

metrics.aggregation: Sum event numerators and denominators within each request over all common layers, compute request means, then arithmetic-mean the 20 request means. Event-weighted values remain secondary.
metrics.uncertainty: Paired bootstrap over the exact 20 test requests, 10000 resamples, seed 20260805; report unrounded two-sided 95% intervals and paired one-sided 95% lower bounds for probe-minus-frequency recall.

decision.continue_probe_to_P2: The probe's K=4/B32 macro-request recall point estimate exceeds frequency and its paired one-sided 95% lower bound for probe-minus-frequency is strictly positive, and the probe point estimate exceeds frequency in all nine K/budget cells.
decision.stop_probe: If the frequency rule fails, preserve the table and stop before conformal calibration.
decision.fold_into_mtp: If MTP dominates probe and both cheaper baselines at equal end-to-end cost, retain the probe only as a refinement candidate inside the MTP-oracle path, not as a separate online mechanism.
decision.shared_correction: Report it in the table but do not revive its rejected serving configuration unless a new completed-time gate independently passes.

mandatory_failures: any held-out value or test-corresponding trace/capture/mapping value opened before the capture/scorer implementation is committed and reviewed, beyond the preserved schema-only incident
any method sees different target events or fixture order
ranking is partial, duplicated, out of range, malformed, or uses non-stable ties
shared correction emits only top-8 while a 16/32/64 cell is claimed

MTP reads any actual future test token, misaligns qj with route position t+j, produces non-nested K prefixes, mutates authoritative state/cache residency/continuation, or omits any target-evaluation/isolation cost
frequency/probe fitting reads precision-diagnostic, calibration, or test rows
reported macro-request metrics are replaced by layer or event weighting
captured production top-8 differs from the scorer's full stable ranking
source, model, scorer, capture, split, or receipt binding differs
claim_limit: This gate measures held-out expert-address prediction on 20 fixed cases. It does not measure NLL, semantic quality, decode throughput, useful-prefetch rate, cache admission benefit, or 1M-context capability.
